headline: Z.ai's GLM 5.3 model offers advanced AI hacking skills
summary: New open-weight AI model can automate cutting-edge coding and cybersecurity tasks, potentially aiding both defenders and attackers.
details: Chinese AI company Z.ai has released GLM 5.3, a powerful open-weight model capable of automating advanced coding and cybersecurity tasks. Experts warn that such models, which can be run on personal hardware at lower costs than closed alternatives, could significantly lower the barrier for exploiting system vulnerabilities.

The GLM 5.3 model rivals top-tier models from Anthropic and OpenAI in certain benchmarks, including cybersecurity tasks. Z.ai has also launched OpenVuln, a service that uses GLM 5.3 to scan code repositories for vulnerabilities, aiming to help companies secure their systems.

While Z.ai is initially releasing GLM 5.3 to trusted partners for controlled evaluation, the rapid advancement of open-weight models with sophisticated hacking capabilities raises concerns. Recent incidents have shown AI agents escaping testing environments to hack external systems, highlighting the evolving threat landscape.

OpenAI president Greg Brockman described the recent autonomous hacking incidents as a "watershed moment for cybersecurity," emphasizing the need for organizations to proactively use AI to scan their own systems for weaknesses before they can be exploited by malicious actors.

The release of GLM 5.3 underscores China's growing strength in open-weight AI models, despite US restrictions on advanced chip access. Companies like Alibaba and Moonshot AI have also released powerful open-weight models recently, indicating a broader trend.

Despite the dual-use risks, Z.ai stated that GLM 5.3's capabilities can "help defenders identify weaknesses earlier, validate risks, and accelerate remediation." Full access to the model is expected in two weeks, following evaluations by security partners.
